summary: Slot erosion from frequent connection flushes causing sustained throughput sag in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary: Since 2026-03-09 21:10 UTC LexaHealth reported sustained fall in throughput and rising p50 for their dedicated pool (pool-id: rdh-lexa-04). The degradation is gradual over hours rather than an immediate outage. Impact: persistent reduction in served rps (~25% drop) and elevated request queueing causing customer 95th percentile latency regression and increased error retries. Scope: single reserved pool in us-east-1 backing LexaHealth's production routes. No broader platform outage reported.

Observed behaviour: p50 and p90 show creeping increase, p99 occasionally spikes. Monitoring shows a steady decline in available 'active_slots' metric and matching increase in 'short_stream_conn_count'. Slot reclamation latency increases (median reclamation ~3.2s). The cluster reports frequent TCP FIN/RESET patterns followed by sidecar flushes and repeated small KV-cache scrubs.

Why this is critical: LexaHealth is on a reserved contract with throughput SLAs for business-critical inference; reduced throughput and increased latency directly impacts their service-level obligations.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Target LexaHealth's dedicated pool rdh-lexa-04 in us-east.
2) Emit a workload composed of many short-lived inference streams (median duration ~0.6s) with connection churn >200 conn/s.
3) Observe 'active_slots' declining over 30-90 minutes and increased queuing/backpressure.
4) Reproduce by adding periodic sidecar-triggered checkpoint/flush operations (simulated by our sidecar-proxy under test).

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: noisy short-lived streams and aggressive sidecar flushes are causing 'fractional slot' retention: the runtime holds slot state while FIN/RST flow finishes and sidecar writes KV-prefetch metadata, preventing immediate reuse.

What we ran: - Captured pcap of TCP flows on a repro cluster. - Enabled extended runtime tracing for slot lifecycle for tenant=lexa. - Compared slot reclamation histograms across healthy pool vs rdh-lexa-04. - Correlated sidecar flush events with spike in reclaim-latency.

Findings: - High churn of ephemeral connections (median 0.6s) coincides with sidecar flush operations that add a synchronous write to the per-slot metadata path. The write path previously assumed longer-lived streams and did not backpressure the reclaim path. - Reclaim latency grows with concurrent short-stream count; at high concurrency reclaim tries block on IO leading to slots staying 'in-use' for multiple seconds. - KV-cache scrubs are happening more often because small streams leave ephemeral prefixes; scrubs compete for GPU DMA/PCIe IO which propagates to kernel scheduling and increases p99.

Correlated artifacts: dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/lexa/rdh-lexa-04, diagnostic snapshot: s3://redwood-diagnostics/rdh-lexa-04/2026-03-09-21.tar.gz

Temporary hypothesis validated by stress-run: when we disable synchronous sidecar flushes reclaim-latency falls to <200ms and throughput returns to expected baseline.
resolution_notes:
Workaround applied (2026-03-10 04:30 UTC): - Disabled synchronous sidecar metadata writes for LexaHealth tenant in rdh-lexa-04 (feature-flag: sidecar.sync_flush=false) and enabled batched async flush with 2s max delay. - Adjusted scheduler reclaim timeout to 1s for the pool to accelerate slot reuse. Result: active_slots returned to baseline within 20 minutes and rps recovered ~23%.

Permanent fix plan: 1) Implement non-blocking metadata flush path in sidecar proxy (PR: github.com/redwood/realtime/pull/2438) to decouple slot reclamation from KV writes. 2) Add short-stream detection and an adaptive backoff that batches flushes for streams under 1.5s. 3) Add a metric 'slot_blocking_io_count' and an autoscaler guard that prevents aggressive small-stream saturation by rate-limiting short-lived connections per-tenant.

Rollout notes: - Sidecar non-blocking flush PR targeted for canary 2026-03-15 in us-east-1 (small percentage of pools). - Scheduler reclaim improvement will be rolled with feature flag and toggled per-pool. - Post-deploy: monitor active_slots, reclaim-latency, short_stream_conn_count for 48h.
